name: Wilhelminapark
title: Ancient Trees in Wilhelminapark, Tilburg: 5 Worth Finding
meta_description: Leonard Springer built this park in the 1890s around trees already there: five registered specimens, from a 150-year-old elm to a rare 1970s oak.
intro: Leonard Springer drew the Wilhelminapark in the 1890s and opened it to the public in May 1898, and part of what makes it worth a visit is that he built around ground that already had trees on it rather than a blank field. Tilburg's oldest elm, on the Dutch national monument register, was standing here before Springer arrived, and a Canadian poplar nearby is older still, from a planting band of 1860 to 1870, decades before the park existed. Springer's own planting survives too: a weeping silver lime he put in himself in 1898, dated to the year in the register's own note, and a flowering ash from the northwest corner that the register admits you can barely see. The fifth tree breaks the pattern entirely. A Pontic oak from the 1970s, a species found wild only in one pocket of northeast Turkey and the Caucasus, is protected not for its age but for what it is, a rarity the register lists under a single word: dendrological. All five stand within a few minutes of each other, free and open daily.
